verdict_reason: Li et al. Eq. 9 defines lambda_(m,n) = log(||delta_(m,n)||/||delta_m||)/(n-m), but _growth_profile exports the undivided log ratio and a regression over normalized depth. In constant-gain 1.15 stacks it returns 0.279524 for two transitions and 1.677143 for twelve, while the paper-defined per-layer value is log(1.15) = 0.139762; perturbation_growth.py:123 also omits the final transformer block, changing live log ratios by 0.326-1.006.
comparable_reason: For matched constant per-block gain, growth_slope and growth_log_ratio equal (L-1) log|a|, giving an exact depth correlation rather than an architecture-free rate. Live current-slice ratios also separate families (GPT-2/DistilGPT-2 2.219/2.158 versus Pythia-70M/160M 5.805/5.603), while restoring the omitted block shifts them another 10.6-17.3%.
github_reason: Fetched arXiv:2503.13530 and searched the exact title, authors, arXiv identifier, and distinctive experiment text; the paper contains no repository link and no author implementation was found. There is no released original code to execute.
paper_reason: The paper gives no numeric QLE scalar: Figure 6 is a qualitative Qwen2-14B convergence/divergence heatmap. Its published 0.27 and 0.075 coefficients describe unperturbed activation-magnitude growth, not QLE, so using them as reproduction targets would be invalid.
confounds_reason: The linear-stack anchor proves exact multiplication by transition count under identical local dynamics, hence direct n_layers confounding. Divergence norms also change under invertible hidden-coordinate rescaling, and the four-model live measurements show a strong architecture-family split.

CODE the task perturbs input embeddings with a random relative-norm direction, whereas Li Eq. 10 defines an elementwise magnitude-adapted perturbation at intermediate layer m; the interventions are not equivalent.
